key_insight: R3MG-C is a high-order algebraic-geometric multilevel preconditioner that improves robustness for continuous finite element systems by building coarse spaces from support-point agglomerates and local polynomial interpolation.
engineering_relevance: It offers a mesh-agnostic, automatic preconditioning strategy for high-order FEM discretizations of elliptic PDEs, where standard AMG often loses efficiency.
method: Recursively partition finite element support points with an R-tree using axis-aligned bounding boxes.
Construct multilevel agglomerates and Galerkin operators without a prescribed mesh hierarchy.
Embed local discontinuous polynomial coarse spaces of degree p'>0 via continuous nodal interpolation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports two- and three-dimensional numerical experiments showing stable V-cycle CG iteration counts, including regimes where standard AMG deteriorates.
watch_item: Performance depends on assumptions such as box regularity, interpolation stability, and stable decomposition, so implementation details and geometric quality may affect robustness.
paper_title: R3MG-C: a high-order algebraic-geometric multilevel preconditioner for continuous finite element discretizations
